title: Regulatory compliance and data controls
task_statement: Map each compliance requirement to a retention, residency, key, or audit control with an owner and evidence. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Retention limits and zero data retention
components.first_principle: The retention arrangement decides how long Anthropic keeps prompts and responses, so it is a design input and not a policy note.

edges.label: no storage at rest after response

steps: Enable ZDR for each organization that handles the regulated data.
Send Messages API calls only with keys from a ZDR-enabled organization.
Check the feature eligibility table before you use a feature with ZDR.
Keep regulated data out of the Console playground, because ZDR does not cover it.
Set the retention period for claude.ai chats in the organization settings.
Use HIPAA readiness for protected health information, but not on Claude Platform on AWS or Microsoft Foundry.
pros: Under ZDR, Anthropic does not store prompts or responses at rest after the response returns.
Uses one setting per organization, which is simple to audit.
Lists the features that ZDR does not cover.
cons: ZDR does not cover the Console, Managed Agents session history, or consumer products.
Under ZDR, the API does not block features that are not eligible, so one call can step outside ZDR.
Covered Models require 30-day retention and are not available under ZDR unless Anthropic authorizes them.
use_when: Prompts contain regulated or confidential data that must not persist.
The workload uses only features that the eligibility table covers.
A contract names ZDR as the arrangement for the data.
do_not_use_when: The workload needs Managed Agents session history or the Console playground.
The workload needs a feature that the eligibility table does not cover. Choose another architecture.

constraints.choice: Enable ZDR per organization and confirm the enablement with the account team.
constraints.combination: Check the feature eligibility table before you enable a new feature.

constraints.choice: Keep ZDR traffic on keys from the ZDR organization only.
constraints.combination: Deploy the forceLoginMethod and forceLoginOrgUUID managed settings to require the ZDR organization for Claude Code.

constraints.choice: Pick a retention period that matches the contract or regulation that applies.
constraints.combination: Use the shortest period that the feature allows. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Expect the Compliance API to skip local sessions under ZDR.
constraints.combination: Record the ZDR decision in the audit file. (Inference)

components.name: Data residency with inference geo and workspace geo
components.first_principle: The request sets where inference runs, and the workspace sets where stored data lives, so each setting controls a different location.

nodes.label: Workspace geo for data at rest

steps: Set inference_geo to us on each request that must run in the United States.
Set default_inference_geo and allowed_inference_geos on the workspace for all of its keys.
Create a workspace with US workspace geo when stored data must stay in the United States.
Read usage.inference_geo in each response to confirm where inference ran.
Expect an error when a request names a geo that the workspace does not allow.
pros: Sets residency on each request, so each call states its location.
Confirms the location in each response.
Blocks requests with a geo outside the workspace list.
cons: US-only inference costs more than global inference.
Workspace geo cannot change after the workspace exists.
Rate limits are shared across all geos.
use_when: A contract or regulation requires US-only inference.
Stored data must stay in one geography.
Several teams need one residency rule that the workspace enforces.
do_not_use_when: The workload accepts global routing, so the price premium adds no value.
The model is earlier than the 4.6 generation, because the inference_geo parameter returns an error there.

constraints.choice: Set inference_geo to us on each request.
constraints.combination: Set allowed_inference_geos to us on the workspace.

constraints.choice: Budget for the US-only price multiplier on all token categories.
constraints.combination: Include cache writes and cache reads in the same budget.

constraints.choice: Plan rate limits with the knowledge that they are shared across all geos.
constraints.combination: Set workspace rate limits for each model.

constraints.choice: Set the residency rule in workspace settings, so application code cannot skip it.
constraints.combination: Use the Admin API data_residency field for automation.

components.name: Customer-managed keys and audit evidence
components.first_principle: A customer key limits who can read new stored data, and the activity feed gives evidence of who accessed what.

edges.label: wraps data keys for new writes
audit logs stay under Anthropic key

steps: Provision a key in the KMS of the platform, such as AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, or Azure Key Vault.
Attach the key to a new workspace before the workspace receives requests, because a later key can take up to a day.
Expect the key to protect data written after it takes effect, not earlier data.
Grant key access only to the Anthropic identifier that the setup guide names.
Create a Compliance Access Key with only the scopes that each reader needs.
Export Activity Feed events to your audit store on a schedule. (Inference)
pros: Keeps key rotation, audit, and revocation under customer control.
Records key operations in the cloud provider audit logs.
Keeps the Activity Feed under the Anthropic key, so audit records survive a key revocation.
cons: CMEK cannot be undone once it is on, and a key loss can cause permanent data loss.
Console playground is disabled on Claude Platform, and chat search is disabled on Claude Enterprise.
Earlier data is not re-encrypted under the customer key.
use_when: The organization must be able to cut access to stored data through the key.
Audit needs a record of who read which records.
do_not_use_when: The team has no process to protect keys from loss.
The feature set needs chat search or Claude Code on the web on Claude Enterprise.

constraints.choice: Use a key in a US region for CMEK, except on Claude Platform on AWS.
constraints.combination: Use an AWS KMS key in the same account and region as the workspace on Claude Platform on AWS.

constraints.choice: Grant key access only to the verified Anthropic identifier.
constraints.combination: Use a key policy, and not an IP allow list, on Claude Platform on AWS.

constraints.choice: Use separate Compliance Access Keys for reads and deletes.
Track CMEK configuration events in the Activity Feed.
constraints.combination: Track key wrap and unwrap events in the cloud provider audit logs.

native_services.text: CMEK uses AWS KMS keys only. The key policy must grant an AWS service principal.

native_services.service: Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed)
native_services.text: CMEK is available with Google Cloud KMS keys for the Anthropic organization that setup creates.
Not in source. The Bedrock page names no CMEK setting for Claude.

components.exam_tie: D5.4. Expect a scenario that asks for customer control over stored data and proof of access. The credited answer combines a CMEK plan, scoped keys, and the Activity Feed. (Inference)
components.trap: A team believes CMEK re-encrypts old data. It protects data written after the key takes effect.
components.decision_rule: Use CMEK for control of new writes, and use the Compliance API for audit evidence.
components.exam_tip: If the scenario asks about data written before the key took effect, state that Anthropic keys still protect that data.
